<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Synthetic\Accessors\Formats;

use Synthetic\Accessors\Accessor;

/** Reads `KEY=value` lines. Blank lines and lines that start with `#` are skipped; a value may be wrapped in one pair of matching quotes. */
final class EnvAccessor implements Accessor
{
    /** @var array<string, string> */
    private array $values = [];

    public function __construct(string $source)
    {
        foreach (preg_split('/\r?\n/', $source) ?: [] as $raw) {
            $line = trim($raw);
            if ($line === '' || str_starts_with($line, '#')) {
                continue;
            }
            $eq = strpos($line, '=');
            if ($eq === false || $eq === 0) {
                continue;
            }
            $key = trim(substr($line, 0, $eq));
            $value = trim(substr($line, $eq + 1));
            if (strlen($value) >= 2 && ($value[0] === '"' || $value[0] === "'") && $value[strlen($value) - 1] === $value[0]) {
                $value = substr($value, 1, -1);
            }
            $this->values[$key] = $value;
        }
    }

    public function get(string $key, ?string $fallback = null): ?string
    {
        return $this->values[$key] ?? $fallback;
    }

    public function has(string $key): bool
    {
        return array_key_exists($key, $this->values);
    }

    public function all(): array
    {
        return $this->values;
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

require __DIR__ . '/../src/Accessor.php';
require __DIR__ . '/../src/Formats/EnvAccessor.php';
require __DIR__ . '/../src/Formats/JsonAccessor.php';

use Synthetic\Accessors\Formats\EnvAccessor;
use Synthetic\Accessors\Formats\JsonAccessor;

$failures = 0;
function check(string $name, bool $ok): void
{
    global $failures;
    echo ($ok ? "ok   " : "FAIL ") . $name . "\n";
    if (!$ok) {
        $failures++;
    }
}

$env = new EnvAccessor("HOST=localhost\nPORT=3000\n");
check('reads KEY=value lines', $env->get('HOST') === 'localhost' && $env->get('PORT') === '3000');

$env = new EnvAccessor("# a comment\n\nKEY=value\n");
check('skips blank lines and comments', $env->all() === ['KEY' => 'value']);

$env = new EnvAccessor("A=\"one two\"\nB='three'\n");
check('strips one pair of matching quotes', $env->get('A') === 'one two' && $env->get('B') === 'three');

$env = new EnvAccessor('KEY=value');
check('answers the fallback for a key that is not there', $env->get('MISSING', 'none') === 'none' && $env->has('KEY') && !$env->has('MISSING'));

$json = new JsonAccessor('{"name":"x","count":3}');
check('json keeps the string values of an object', $json->all() === ['name' => 'x']);

exit($failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);

input.title: EnvAccessor strips a leading `export` plus spaces or tabs before any other line check, in both packages
input.rationale: `export KEY=value` must give the key `KEY`, exactly as if the prefix were absent. So the prefix (`^export[ \t]+`, after trimming the line) is removed first, before the blank-line, `#`-comment and `=` checks, in `packages/js` and `packages/php` alike (ADR-1). Only a space or tab may follow `export`: JS `\s` is Unicode-aware and PHP `\s` is ASCII-only, so `[ \t]` keeps the two packages identical. A bare `export`, `exportFOO=x`, `export=x`, `export NOEQUALS` and `export =x` are therefore not treated as prefixed assignments, and a `#` line stays a comment even when it mentions `export`. Both packages gained the same two tests.
input.alternatives: Use `\s+` after `export`: rejected, it behaves differently in JS (Unicode whitespace) and PHP (ASCII) and breaks parity. Strip `export` only after the comment and blank checks: rejected, `export # x=1` would then not behave as `# x=1` would, against "exactly as if the prefix were not there". Strip any `export` substring or an `export` without a following space: rejected, it would turn the legitimate keys `exportHOST` and `export` into something else. Change only the JS package: rejected by ADR-1, the gap is the defect.

content.text:
`EnvAccessor` now accepts `export KEY=value` and reads the key as `KEY`. I made the change in both the JS and PHP packages, because ADR-1 requires a behavior change in one to be made in the other in the same change. Both test suites pass: JS 8/8 and PHP 7/7.

- **Rule:** the accessor strips a leading `export` followed by spaces or tabs before any other check. A line like `export # note` stays a comment, and `export  PORT = 3000` reads as `PORT=3000`. The edits are in `env-accessor.ts` and `EnvAccessor.php`.
- **Not a prefix:** `exportHOST=a`, `export=b` and a bare `export` keep their old meaning. `export NOEQUALS` and `export =c` are skipped, and `# export X=1` is still a comment.
- **Why spaces and tabs only:** JS `\s` matches Unicode whitespace and PHP `\s` only ASCII, so `[ \t]` keeps the two packages identical.
